intro.title: Overview
intro.body:
Frontend-heavy Full-Stack Engineer with 5 years of experience building enterprise websites, product platforms, ERP systems, and interactive web experiences.

My primary expertise is in Vue, Nuxt, React, TypeScript, JavaScript, and Node.js, with additional experience in GSAP, Three.js, and creative coding. I enjoy translating complex requirements into maintainable systems while balancing performance, usability, and interaction.

Beyond implementation, I work closely with designers, PMs, and backend engineers, and have experience taking ownership of product planning, technical architecture, and long-term system improvement.

work.title: PROJECTS
work.summary: Selected work across product development, enterprise systems, creative frontend, and interactive web experiences.
work.description: Over the past 5 years, I’ve delivered 30+ web projects, from large-scale corporate websites and ERP systems to exhibition microsites and interactive digital experiences. I enjoy working at the intersection of frontend engineering, motion, and interaction—building experiences that are visually engaging, performant, and maintainable.

projects.title: Pay La (Shared Expense Web App)
projects.description: Mobile-first shared expense and settlement web application built with Next.js, Firebase.
highlight: Next.js static export with GitHub Pages

detail.title: Pay La
body: Pay La is a mobile-first shared expense web app designed to make tracking group spending, splitting expenses, and settling balances simple and transparent.

Users can create shared groups, invite members, record expenses with equal, exact amount, or percentage-based splits, view calculated balances, and record settlements. Google Sign-In and real-time group data are handled through Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore.

The financial logic is separated from the UI and Firebase layer through deterministic split and balance engines. Resolved expense shares are stored as historical financial records, while group balances are derived from expenses and settlements rather than maintained as a separate source of truth.
The application is built with Next.js, React, and TypeScript, supports Traditional Chinese and English, and uses Next.js static export for deployment through GitHub Pages with a custom domain.

projects.title: Enterprise ERP Management System
projects.description: Multi-module ERP platform for sales, purchasing, inventory, transactions, and eSign workflows
highlight: Connected sales, purchasing, inventory, and transaction workflows
Reusable admin components and document architecture
Quotation PDF and public eSign workflow

detail.title: Enterprise ERP Management System
body: Enterprise ERP Management System is a multi-module internal operations platform covering sales quotations, purchasing, inventory movement, transaction records, and digital signing workflows.

The frontend architecture uses shared DataTable, Modal, Selector, AutoForm, and PDF document patterns across multiple ERP modules, while API access is organized through reusable service composables to keep complex workflows consistent and maintainable.

A key feature is the quotation and eSign flow, where internal users can generate public signing links, customers can complete handwritten signature or email OTP verification, and the backend produces a signed PDF for cloud storage and later access.
The system also provides separate Admin, Business, and public eSign experiences, with route, menu, and action-level permission control based on different user roles.

projects.title: Goodbye 1987 (Interactive Film Website)
projects.description: Interactive promotional website built with Nuxt, GSAP, and p5.js
highlight: Generative visuals and animations with p5.js
Interactive quiz with downloadable image & video results

detail.title: Goodbye 1987
body: Goodbye 1987 is an interactive promotional website created for a film project, combining cinematic storytelling with motion-driven web interactions.
The experience features horizontal scroll sequences, GSAP-controlled transitions, and p5.js-generated visuals, including animated graphic elements and interactive effects.

A key part of the project is an interactive quiz that generates personalized visual results, including downloadable images and video content, extending the experience beyond a conventional promotional website.

projects.alt: Goodbye 1987 interactive film website project image

detail.title: Sino-French War
body: Sino-French War is an interactive historical storytelling website created for the National Museum of Taiwan History, combining 3D scenes, complex motion design, and scroll-driven narrative sequences.

The experience is structured as a long-form digital story, using animated transitions, layered visual elements, and 3D interactions to guide users through historical events while maintaining a continuous narrative flow.

I joined the project during development, completed the latter half of the frontend implementation, and focused on performance optimization, animation stability, and refining complex interactive sequences across the experience.

detail.title: Generative Art Collection
body: An ongoing collection of nearly 70 p5.js sketches exploring generative art, interactive graphics, and browser-based visual experiments.
The works experiment with trigonometry, geometric systems, procedural motion, particle behavior, 3D graphics, and shader-based rendering to create evolving visual compositions and interactions.

Rather than a single project, the collection serves as a continuous creative coding practice for exploring mathematical patterns, visual systems, animation techniques, and real-time graphics in the browser.

detail.title: Far Eastern New Century
body: Far Eastern New Century is a large-scale multilingual corporate website developed by Block Studio, with a complex enterprise content structure spanning more than 90 pages.
My work focused on frontend implementation, reusable components and page templates, multilingual content handling, and maintaining consistency across a large number of corporate content pages.
The project also included accessibility improvements, frontend optimization, and security remediation work to support long-term stability and maintainability.

projects.title: Bai Bai 1.0 (CMS + Animation)
projects.description: Content-driven site built with WordPress + Nuxt

detail.title: Bai Bai 1.0
body: Bai Bai 1.0 is a content-driven website developed by Block Studio, combining WordPress CMS with a Nuxt frontend and GSAP-based motion.
The project focused on integrating multilingual content from WordPress, building animated SVG and interface transitions, and maintaining a stable content workflow across the site.
The frontend also involved optimization work within an existing project structure, improving maintainability and supporting continued updates without disrupting the established CMS workflow.
